summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplant was admitted for constipation lasting five days, following a recent hospitalization for varicella infection. She had decreased oral intake, abdominal discomfort, and one episode of vomiting after attempting laxatives. Initial imaging showed air-fluid levels, but CT scan ruled out bowel obstruction. A gastric emptying study revealed delayed gastric emptying with 30% retention at four hours. The ileus was attributed to recent immobility and codeine use rather than diabetic gastroparesis. She was managed with IV fluids, bowel regimen, and metoclopramide. Her renal function improved from a creatinine of 1.2 to 0.9 with rehydration. She gradually resumed oral intake, passed stool, and was discharged home on a regimen including senna, Miralax, docusate, metoclopramide, pantoprazole, and misoprostol, with instructions to follow up with GI and monitor for worsening symptoms.
